method: Fixed before reading: prior reactions set size (median |move|, cross-checked against 20d realised vol); direction comes only from run-up versus what is plausibly priced, plus reaction-sign momentum. Zacks-style previews are legible and assumed priced. Default Neutral unless two independent signals align.
key_drivers: +10.2% in five sessions into a bmo print, arriving 5.6% from the 52w high and +58% off the low
Reaction base rate skews negative: 5 of last 8 prints sold off despite a strong operating record
Forward P/S 6.99x, the richest in its aerospace/defence peer set - a high bar to clear
Zacks Rank 3 with a near-zero +0.36% ESP: no positive-surprise tilt to offset the raised bar
Both directional signals point the same way, which is why this is the batch's cleanest setup
what_would_change_my_mind: If the 10% five-day rally traced to a specific pre-announced contract award rather than earnings positioning, the priced-in argument would weaken sharply.
reasoning: This is the one name where both of my pre-committed directional inputs agree. Curtiss-Wright routinely delivers good quarters and the stock routinely fades them - five negative reactions in eight - and it enters this print after a 10% five-day rally at a premium multiple, so the operational bar is high and the sentiment bar higher. The peer article confirms a rich 6.99x forward P/S and only a token +0.36% ESP on a Rank 3, so there is no surprise tilt working the other way. Sizing stays modest: 41.7% realised vol is about 2.6% daily and the historical median is 3.45%, giving roughly 4.2%. Medium certainty; the reaction-fade pattern is consistent but the effect is small.
